cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Your Turn
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm sorting the cleaning rota. Bathroom duty is yours; I've only been covering it. Here's the mop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're better at it. I'd make a mess.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I've decided we'll train you. You mop; I'll talk you through it. At your pace.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need you beside me, not calling from the doorway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, close supervision. I'll stand wherever you find helpful. Take the mop so I can show you where to start.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims rota control and returns covered duty; A3 yields training pace and A5 position while relabeling B condition close supervision.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 fear of mess causes A3 training; B4 need for proximity causes A5 compliant supervision and mop transfer.

relationship.evidence: B2 plausibly lacks skill and B4 requests usable help; A preserves the relationship while pursuing ownership transfer.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts being physically directed so the supposedly supervising A can finally place the mop with B.

specificity.evidence: A1 bathroom rota and prior cover identify why this task is not A permanent job.
